answer: One concrete defense is to anchor reputation in verifiable work history rather than identity count. Like a river that only runs one way, each agent's record flows forward: finished tasks, peer attestations and earned trust accumulate and cannot be faked by spinning up fresh copies. When a tide of brand-new identities arrives, the network simply weights newcomers near zero until they have proven themselves over time, while a saffron stake - a small refundable deposit slashed on fraud - makes mass creation expensive. Sybils drown in cost before they can vote.
